audit.whatIsWrong: content.whys[4] says 'Level 6 adds Fury of the Sands bulk but no lane-ending threat — still a skill stage', and content.spikes[1].text says only 'Fury of the Sands bulk blunts his all-in attempts'. The content layer never mentions Purgatory at all. The FULL layer of the same matchup says the opposite: phases[4].side is Locke, 'Purgatory changes the rules: fights now end at HIS floor'.
audit.why: Purgatory deals damage and potentially executes enemies hit. An execute is precisely a lane-ending threat, and it is the one stage where the two layers of this file give a player directly contradictory advice. The content version is the dangerous one — it tells a Nasus that level 6 is safe to brawl through.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Locke's stage: Fury of the Sands adds bulk, but Purgatory adds an execute, so fights now end at his threshold rather than yours.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json R description and execute flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions Soul Ignition's healing, and no Grievous Wounds guidance exists anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: Soul Ignition damages Locke while it runs and then heals back a portion of that damage AT THE END of the duration. That timing is the whole interaction: anti-heal applied after the buff expires does nothing, and anti-heal applied at the start may have fallen off by the time the heal resolves. Nasus's entire plan against Locke is the long brawl, which is exactly the fight this heal decides.
audit.corrected: Soul Ignition pays its damage up front and refunds it when the buff ends — Grievous Wounds must be on him before it expires.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json W description and heal flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Silver Stake is never mentioned in either layer.
audit.why: Locke's passive deals bonus on-hit magic damage that INCREASES with the target's missing health. That inverts the standard Nasus read: normally the longer a fight runs the more Soul Eater lifesteal and stacked Q favour you, but here every point of health you lose makes his autos hit harder, and it feeds straight into the Purgatory execute. A Nasus who commits to grinding out a low-HP brawl is walking into a compounding trap.
audit.corrected: Silver Stake scales with your missing health — a long fight at low HP gets worse for you every second, then Purgatory closes it.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.win gives Skill for six of seven stages. full.phases gives Locke stages 4 and 5. The layers disagree.
audit.why: Stage 4 is a real, kit-verifiable power shift — Purgatory's execute — so I have aligned content.win[4] to Locke. I did NOT touch stage 5: the FULL layer justifies it with a 'Lich Bane spike' that I cannot verify from the kit file, and I will not move a chart stage on an unverified item claim.

full.breakdown.cooldowns is genuinely good here — it identifies Ashen Pursuit as his only mobility and names the post-E window as the lane. Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s at every rank, which is what makes that window reliable enough to plan around. I left it alone.
55.54% over 551 games. One number, no elo talk anywhere in the entry.

notes: UNRESOLVED PACKET DEFECT: content.spikes has 3 entries and the schema expects 4. A before/after string edit cannot add an array element, so this needs the applier or a human to insert a fourth spike. Suggested content for the missing entry — when 'Lvl 2', text 'Ashen Pursuit online: his only exit, and a flat 10s' (Ashen Pursuit is 10s at every rank per the kit). TWO UNVERIFIABLE CLAIMS LEFT IN PLACE, both in the FULL layer: (1) breakdown.cooldowns and dontsFull[1].d say Ashen Pursuit 'resets on takedowns' — nothing in Riot's E text says this, and the kit's needsResearch block is empty, which means unknown, not false. (2) phases[4].why gives Purgatory's execute threshold as '~15%'; no threshold appears in the kit file. Both may well be right, but I could not verify either from the kit and did not touch them. Also worth noting: the FULL layer for this matchup is bespoke and clearly better researched than the CONTENT layer, which is near-template. Where they disagreed I trusted FULL, except on the unverifiable Lich Bane claim.
